issues.legal_issue: The government may withdraw land from acquisition before taking possession without first hearing the landowner.
material_facts: Acquisition notifications and notices had been issued, but the government had not taken possession of the land.
The government withdrew the land from acquisition and did not give the owner an opportunity to be heard beforehand.
issues.conclusion: The government could withdraw unilaterally before taking possession, and no hearing for the owner had to be implied.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4, 6 and 9 of the Land Acquisition Act, the notifications and notices do not divest the owner of rights in the land; section 16 provides that title vests in the government only when possession is taken. Section 48 permits withdrawal before possession, and the court held that this power may be exercised unilaterally. It relied on Trustees of Bai Smarth Jain Shvetamber Murtipujak Gyanodhyaya Trust v. State of Gujarat, AIR 1981 Gujarat 107.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated proceedings to acquire land.
predicates.possession_not_taken: The government had not taken possession of the land when it withdrew from acquisition.

issues.definition: When acquisition proceedings are underway and the government has not taken possession, the government may withdraw unilaterally.

issues.legal_issue: The government need not continue an acquisition or provide cogent reasons for abandoning it when it has not taken possession of the land.
material_facts: The government had not taken possession of the land, so the owner retained its rights and responsibility to care for it.
The land had become extensively occupied by slum dwellers, making the intended housing project impracticable.
The owner sought an order requiring the government to proceed with acquisition, take possession and pay compensation.
issues.conclusion: The government could not be compelled to continue the acquisition, and it was not required to give cogent reasons for deciding not to proceed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 16 and 48 of the Land Acquisition Act leave ownership with the owner until possession is taken and allow withdrawal before then. The court considered that section 48(2) provides compensation for damage or costs caused by acquisition proceedings, and analogized to the principle in specific performance that a person is not compelled to acquire land where damages can compensate for the breach. Section 24 concerns the basis for assessing compensation and does not require the government to take over the land. The court also referred to M/s. Majas Land Development Corpn. v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1983 Bombay 188.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated proceedings to acquire land.
predicates.possession_not_taken: The government had not taken possession of the land when the issue arose.
predicates.owner_seeks_forced_acquisition: The owner sought to require the government to complete the acquisition and take the land.

issues.definition: If the government has not taken possession in an acquisition proceeding and the owner seeks to force completion, the government need not continue the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: Withdrawing from an acquisition after a court challenge is not mala fide when genuine circumstances make the intended use of the land impracticable.
material_facts: The government withdrew from acquisition after the owner had filed a court petition seeking completion of the acquisition.
Extensive slum encroachments had made it impracticable to use the land for the intended housing purpose.
The government relied on those circumstances in withdrawing from the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The withdrawal was not mala fide; the timing of the decision after the court petition did not establish bad faith in light of the genuine circumstances supporting withdrawal.
issues.legal_principle: Even assuming a withdrawal under section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act must be bona fide and supported by reasons, the court found the stated practical impediments genuine. It held that the government was not responsible for the trespassers’ occupation and was not required to proceed when the intended purpose could not be achieved. The court also observed that proceeding despite clear knowledge that the land could not serve its intended purpose could itself be mala fide.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated proceedings to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.withdrawal_after_court_challenge: The government withdrew from acquisition after the owner challenged the delay or sought completion in court.
predicates.extensive_encroachments_make_intended_us: Extensive occupation of the land made it impracticable to carry out the intended public use.

issues.definition: A withdrawal after a court challenge is not mala fide when extensive encroachments make the intended use impracticable.

issues.legal_issue: An owner who suffers damage or incurs costs because of acquisition proceedings may claim compensation when the government withdraws before taking possession.
material_facts: The government withdrew the land from acquisition before taking possession.
The court recognized that the owner could have suffered damage or incurred costs because of the acquisition proceedings.
The owner had been asked to provide details of any compensation claim for consideration under the law.
issues.conclusion: The owner could pursue a claim for compensation for damage or costs resulting from the acquisition proceedings, and the government was to dispose of that claim in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48(2) of the Land Acquisition Act provides compensation for damage suffered or costs incurred in consequence of acquisition proceedings when the government withdraws. The court also noted that M/s. Majas Land Development Corpn. v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1983 Bombay 188, had recognized liability to pay compensation under section 48(2).

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated proceedings to acquire land.
predicates.withdrawal_before_possession: The government withdrew from acquisition before taking possession of the land.
predicates.owner_suffered_proceeding_related_loss: The owner suffered damage or incurred costs as a result of the acquisition proceedings.

issues.definition: An owner may claim compensation for proceeding-related loss when the government withdraws from an acquisition before taking possession.
